title: SeamRegistry
description: Source of truth: repo/process artifact (Category C — no DHT entry type, per the seam-concern-contract-architecture plan's Non-goals). A per-crate `seam-registry.yaml` conforming to this schema is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for that crate's decision surface: every pure decision predicate, verdict fn, boundary answer type, and reason/outcome enum, plus the concern classes (C0-C14, C6 split into C6a/C6b) each one answers and the contract test(s) that pin its behaviour. The census (`placement-audit.py --epr-meta`, P3.2) and the concern x seam matrix (P4.3) are DERIVED READ-MODELS over this file — never hand-authored. 'Seam' here names a crate/module locus (this registry's own vocabulary), NOT the concern-routing atlas's composition seams or participation tracks — those are matrix vocabulary (surface 6), not registry vocabulary. Each row in `decisionPoints` is deliberately SELF-CONTAINED (no cross-row references) because the census loads and validates rows one at a time and a single malformed row must flag itself without emptying the registered set (the EprRouter poisoned-scope lesson: fail-closed `collect` over rows degrades to silence, never total loss).

seamRegistryVersion.description: Schema-compatibility version of this registry file, independent of the schema's own draft version. Bump when a row's shape changes in a way old census tooling could misread.

crate.description: The Rust package name exactly as declared in the owning Cargo.toml's `[package] name`. NOT necessarily the directory name — e.g. doorway-service's package name is `doorway`, and the content_store zome's crate name is `content_store`. The census resolves this against Cargo.toml, not the file path, to catch drift.

crateRoot.description: Repo-relative path (no leading/trailing slash) to the crate's root directory (the one containing its Cargo.toml), e.g. 'elohim/elohim-storage' or 'doorway/doorway-service'. Disambiguates crate-name collisions and anchors every row's sourceLocation.file as relative-to-this-root.

seamLocus.description: One to a few sentences naming the crate/module-level locus this registry covers (e.g. 'head-election and canonical-move decision surface in the P2P projection-reconcile + head-adoption pipeline'). A description of WHERE the decision points live, not a restatement of the atlas's composition-seam or participation-track vocabulary — those are matrix concerns (surface 6), not this file's.

decisionPoints.description: Every registered pure decision predicate, verdict fn, boundary answer type, and reason/outcome enum this crate exposes. Convention over macros: a YAML row plus (eventually) a naming-convention lint — no proc-macro, no registration-by-attribute.

concernId.description: A concern class id from the canon (C0-C14; C6 splits into C6a bounded-work / C6b idempotent-effect). The canon's own text is the definition; this registry only cites ids, it does not restate guarantees.

concernBindingStatus.description: How this decision point stands with respect to the cited concern TODAY (an architectural claim, re-verified at census time, not a permanent grade). 'answered' = the point's logic demonstrably enforces the concern's guarantee and a contract test pins it. 'partial' = the logic exists but a real gap remains (e.g. correct in isolation but unbound at its call site — dead code, zero production callers). 'unbound' = the concern SHOULD apply at this decision point (it is the definitional question here) but no guard or rule currently answers it. 'n-a' = on inspection this concern does not actually apply to this point; REQUIRES justification so the row cannot silently opt out of a concern the matrix would otherwise expect.

justification.description: Required when status is 'n-a', 'unbound', or 'partial' — the honesty this schema exists to enforce: a decision point that looks concern-relevant may not silently claim full coverage. Optional (but welcome) when status is 'answered'.

file.description: Path to the source file, relative to the registry's `crateRoot` (e.g. 'src/services/head_adoption.rs').

modulePath.description: Rust module path to the item, e.g. 'services::head_adoption::decide_head_action' or 'content_diesel::StaleReason'. Omit only when the item is a private free function with no meaningful external path (still cite the symbol name in `name`).

line.description: 1-indexed line of the item's definition at authoring time. A LINE HINT, not a pin — it drifts as the file is edited; the census resolves by symbol name/grep, never trusts this number blindly (spot-check-the-measure discipline).

path.description: Repo-relative path (from the repo root, NOT crateRoot, since sweettests commonly live outside the crate) to the file containing the test. MUST be a Rust source file: the census resolves a citation by grepping `fn <testName>(` in this file, so a non-`.rs` path can only ever resolve to 'test not found' — a citation that reads as a gap while looking like proof. This is the pattern's whole job; see `testName` for where a2o/Gherkin evidence goes instead.

testName.description: The exact `fn` name of the test (or, for a table/property test asserting many cases, the one enclosing `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` fn). Must be a REAL, currently-passing test — cite only tests that exist; a name that does not resolve at census time is exactly the phantom-validator failure mode this plan exists to stop (C7). The identifier pattern is deliberate and is NOT a placeholder for prose: this field is a symbol the census resolves, never a description of what is proved (that is `summary`/`notes`). AN A2O SCENARIO IS NOT CITED HERE. Gherkin evidence joins a decision surface through the habit register — the scenario's `@concern:<tag>`, the habit's `checks:` in `genesis/manifests/habits.yaml`, and the seam's `habits:` in the seam catalog — which is the granularity a feature-level `@concern:` tag actually has (a seam column, not one row). Citing it here would be a second, weaker home for a join that already exists, and would resolve to nothing. Put the pointer in the row's `notes` if a reader needs it.

kind.description: unit = #[cfg(test)] mod in the same source file, no conductor/network. sweettest = Holochain SweetConductor multi-agent test (elohim/holochain/tests/sweettest). integration = crosses a process/HTTP boundary but is not a sweettest (e.g. wiremock-backed doorway tests).

mirrorRisk.description: Optional self-flag: true if this test computes its expected value via the SAME helper/formula the code under test uses (the anti-mirror hazard P3.2's fixture targets — a passing test can be measuring the mirror, not the behaviour). Leave false/omitted when the test's expectation is an independently-stated literal or a different derivation path.

name.description: The symbol's own name — a fn name (e.g. 'decide_head_action') or a type name (e.g. 'StaleReason'). Exactly one decision point per row; a fn and its own return-type enum are two separate rows if both are independently registrable (e.g. `decide_reconcile` the fn and `ReconcileDecision` the enum it returns may each carry their own concern bindings and test citations).

kind.description: pure-decision-predicate = a side-effect-free fn mapping inputs to a decision (testable with no conductor/pool/network/peer). verdict-fn = a fn that additionally carries authority semantics over a proposed move/claim (may still be pure; the label marks its role, e.g. canonical_move_verdict, an authorization gate). boundary-answer-type = an enum/struct that IS the decision outcome returned across a boundary (a decide fn's return type, an extern's Option<T>, an HTTP-facing outcome type). reason-outcome-enum = a typed reason/label vocabulary consumed by metrics or callers to explain WHY a boundary-answer-type landed where it did (e.g. StaleReason, DeferReason, SsrFallbackReason). state-transition = a fn whose registrable claim is the SHAPE OF ITS EFFECT on longer-lived shared state — replace-not-append, upsert-not-insert, converge-not-accrete — rather than any value it returns (it typically returns a count or unit, and never a verdict). The other four kinds are all decision shapes; this one exists because C6a/C6b declare `probe_home: seam-registry` and name effectful surfaces ('boot re-projection', '(id,target) keyed work') that no decision shape can host — an instrument blind to the class it is the declared probe home for. ADMISSION IS NARROW, and the narrowness is the point: register a fn here only when re-application is a DESIGNED property (a retry-until-registered boot loop, a periodic manifest refresh, a reconcile tick) AND a contract test pins the invariant across REPEATED or CONCURRENT application rather than a single call's return. That repeat-application pin is what makes this a kind instead of 'any fn that writes'; a fn whose only claim is that it wrote the row is not a decision surface and does not belong in this registry at all. A write whose registrable claim is a verdict ABOUT the write (admit/reject — K2Store::put_at -> K2PutOutcome, TransportManifestStore::accept_at -> AcceptOutcome) stays a verdict-fn; this kind is for the write whose claim is about the write itself.

concernIds.description: Every concern class this decision point's design makes a claim about today (answered, partial, unbound, or n-a-with-justification). This is an ARCHITECTURAL CLAIM the row's author derived from the plan's canon table — conservative tagging only: tag what the code demonstrably does today, not what it is aspirationally meant to do (an aspiration belongs in a 'partial'/'unbound' justification, not an 'answered' status).

contractTests.description: The real, currently-existing test(s) that pin this decision point's behaviour. MUST be `null` (never an empty array, never omitted) when no test exists yet — an explicit, honest gap the census (P3.2) is meant to flag, not a silently-absent field. When null, `gapNote` is REQUIRED.

gapNote.description: Required when `contractTests` is null: a one-to-two-sentence honest note on why no contract test exists yet (e.g. 'no direct unit or sweettest exercises this extern; only reachable indirectly through X, which is not the same claim'). Optional free-form commentary otherwise.

summary.description: Optional one-line statement of what decision this point makes (the matrix and census render this; keep it a single sentence).

notes.description: Optional free-form context: forcing incidents, forecast-row ties, known dead-code status, etc. Prefer `gapNote` for the specific no-test case.
